public_rationale: Read fairly, the claim is that within three months of the post, matching Anthropic on revenue would require an annualized run rate of about $60 billion. The window ends on 2026-11-18, after the evaluation date. As a progress marker, OpenAI's run rate was reported at about $50 billion net at the end of September (e1). The two companies count partner revenue differently (e2), which matters for any parity benchmark. No decisive event has settled it early.
limitations: Relies on secondary reporting of run rates.
Whether the claim is supported depends on how 'compete' and the gross/net basis are read.

our_interpretation: 'Compete' here means keeping revenue parity with Anthropic, as his context makes clear. It does not mean merely staying a big rival.

This is a requirement claim. The testable part is that within three months of the post, revenue parity with Anthropic will require an annualized run rate of about $60 billion. In other words, Anthropic's run rate on a comparable basis will be at or near $60 billion or more by then.
The deadline is three months after the 2026-08-18 post: 2026-11-18.
'To compete with Anthropic' is a purpose clause, not an event that has to happen first, so no antecedent needs checking.
criteria.support_condition: By 2026-11-18, reliable reporting shows Anthropic's run rate on a basis comparable to OpenAI's at about $60 billion or more, so parity would need roughly $60 billion.
criteria.contradiction_condition: By 2026-11-18, Anthropic's comparable run rate is clearly below $60 billion, so OpenAI could match it without reaching $60 billion.
